text: Chapters one through three built the concepts. Starting right now, every lesson is real PySpark code — welcome to Chapter 4.

Here's creating a DataFrame from a list of tuples, with an explicit schema. Unlike Lesson 22's read CSV, where Pandas just guesses types, here you're stating the schema yourself — string, integer, double. That matters more in Spark, where a wrong guess across genuinely distributed data is far more expensive to catch later.
You can also build one from a list of dictionaries — Lesson 15's exact shape, again. Spark infers the schema automatically here, the same way Pandas did back in Lesson 21.
And for quick testing, spark dot range makes a tiny DataFrame instantly — one column, I-D, zero through nine. No real data needed at all, and several labs in this chapter use exactly this.
Tuples with an explicit schema, dictionaries with inference, or range for a quick test. Next lesson: reading the real NYC Taxi file, in actual PySpark. See you there.
